notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Monday 23 November (EGX30 50,711.96); Tuesday's session has not opened. Brent and gold are Tuesday-morning Asian-trading prices; Wall Street is Monday's close. The pound is the six-bank average at midday Monday reported by Amwal Al Ghad. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Tuesday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Monday's net flows by nationality, because Amwal Al Ghad reports Egyptians as net buyers of EGP 2.41 bn and foreigners as net sellers of EGP 2.45 bn, while EnterpriseAM reports local investors as the only net sellers; a CBE dollar rate (54.31 buy and 54.44 sell appear only in a summary of EnterpriseAM's page); Tuesday's Kospi gain (6.17% per Investing.com, 7% at 04:15 GMT per Al Jazeera); Monday's advancing and declining stocks; the IRGC's account of three tankers hitting mines, which Al Jazeera reports as Iran's claim. Egypt Aluminum's 17 November row on StockAnalysis remains inconsistent (a -0.30% change against a 5.2% fall in the closes).

items: The EGX30 drops 2.85% to 49,989.79 on Sunday and small caps fall 5.55%, as local investors sell after Wall Street's correction → foreigners are the only net buyers; turnover stays 40.4% below its 90-day average.
Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt divert to Europe, and fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas at $12.75/mmBtu → Europe outbids Cairo for scarce cargoes, raising costs for energy-hungry industry.
US stock futures jump 2.2% on Monday after the S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday into a correction → a rebound abroad could steady the EGX after Sunday's sell-off.
Tankers are set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery → Gulf attacks keep oil's risk premium alive; Brent holds near $92.7.
Iran strikes US air-defence sites in Bahrain and tankers are hit near Hormuz on Saturday → the Gulf war widens, keeping oil, shipping and insurance risk high for Egypt.
Goldman Sachs sees the CBE holding at 20% until late Q1 2027, then cutting 700 bp by 2028 → it calls the pound more than 30% undervalued and sees no external financing gap through FY2029/30.
Misr Life Insurance, which earned EGP 5.8 bn in 2025, targets a 70% payout ahead of its EGX debut in early December → a large, high-dividend state listing deepens the market.
Orascom Construction breaks ground on Jordan's $6.7 bn Aqaba-Amman water project → the project adds to its backlog before its merger shares list on 24 November.
Wall Street enters a correction: the Nasdaq falls 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.5% on Friday as the AI sell-off deepens → a global risk-off mood can weigh on emerging markets, including the EGX on Sunday.
Gold posts its worst week in eight months, down 8.9%, and 21K gold in Egypt drops 3.04% to EGP 5,575 → markets bet on a December Fed hike, and margin calls force sales.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh as Gulf war-risk costs climb → tanker insurance from the Middle East to Asia reaches $12.29 a barrel, keeping Red Sea and Suez risk high.
Arab Energy Fund launches a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → a Gulf-backed buyer puts a price on an EGX-listed oil services firm.
An AI-led sell-off hits markets: the Nasdaq falls 2.3% on Thursday and Asian indices drop up to 6.8% on Friday → Anthropic's record IPO does not calm AI-bubble fears.
Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027 → higher pay supports spending but raises costs for labour-heavy firms.
The EGX30 slips 0.17% to 51,458.04 as Telecom Egypt falls 3.47% → turnover is 43.9% below the 90-day average.
Gold drops to a 14-month low of $3,554 and heads for a 9% weekly loss → markets price a 97.3% chance of a Fed hike in December.

The IMF reaches a staff-level agreement on Egypt's final EFF review and third RSF review, worth about $2.3 bn → board approval before 15 December would close the programme and support the pound and Egypt's credit standing.
Egypt's economy grows 4.9% in July to September, up from 4.7%, while unemployment rises to 6.0% → growth holds up despite the war, rate hike and gas cuts.
Orascom Construction's nine-month profit nearly doubles to $218 mn as its backlog reaches $11.6 bn → strong awards support the stock ahead of the OCI merger listing on 24 November.
Gold falls 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025; 21K in Egypt drops to EGP 5,750 → Fed minutes show almost all officials see more hikes ahead.

stories.h: EGX30 rebounds 1.44% as small caps jump 3.4%
stories.what: The EGX30 rises 1.44% to 50,711.96 on Monday, the EGX70 3.41% and the EGX100 2.81%; market cap returns to EGP 4.00 tn. Turnover is EGP 7.1 bn, 36.1% below the 90-day average, and the index is up 21.2% this year. Palm Hills (+4.7%), Misr Cement (+4.6%) and Alexandria Containers (+2.9%) lead the gainers; Emaar Misr (-0.8%) is the main loser.
stories.why: The rebound follows Sunday's 2.85% fall as global markets steady.
stories.aff: Blue chips, banks and small caps.
stories.eg: Buyers return after Sunday's sell-off, though turnover stays thin.
stories.names: Palm Hills, Credit Agricole Egypt, QNB Egypt (up); Emaar Misr (down).

key.l: Misr Life valuation at the IPO range

stories.h: Misr Life opens its IPO book below its adviser's fair value
stories.what: Misr Insurance Holding offers 750 mn existing Misr Life shares, or 15%, at EGP 12.00 to 13.60 each, valuing the insurer at EGP 60 to 68 bn; adviser BDO puts fair value at EGP 13.82. Institutions bid for 712.5 mn shares until Friday and the public for 37.5 mn until next Monday. The final price is due Saturday and trading around Thursday 3 December. Misr Life earned EGP 5.17 bn in the first half of 2026, and the offer can be upsized to 20%.
stories.why: The state is selling part of a large insurer through Misr Insurance Holding.
stories.aff: Insurance, the EGX's depth and state divestments.
stories.eg: A large, profitable insurer joins the market at a discount to fair value.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokers and liquidity; may draw cash from other stocks while books are open.

stories.h: Nasdaq posts its best day since April 2025 as Nvidia brings back Huang
stories.what: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he resigned, and its shares rise 31.5%. The Nasdaq Composite jumps 6.5% to 24,089.56, the S&P 500 4.7% to 7,251.69 and the Dow 3% to 49,598.97. On Tuesday Taiwan's index rises about 9%. The US adds Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian firms to its export blacklist.
stories.why: Huang's return revives the AI trade after last week's rout.
stories.aff: Global tech stocks and emerging-market risk appetite.
stories.eg: Calmer global markets support flows into Egyptian assets.

stories.h: Brent hits a three-month low as Libya restarts a key pipeline
stories.what: Brent falls $3.20, or 3.46%, to settle at $89.37 on Monday, its lowest close since 31 August, and slips to $88.71 on Tuesday morning. WTI settles at $80.17. Libya's Sharara pipeline restarts and Middle East supplies rise; JPMorgan sees oil in the high $70s in the first half of 2027. OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November. Separately, Iraq weighs supplying Egypt with 10 mn barrels of crude, with no price agreed.
stories.why: Rising supply outweighs shipping risks in the Gulf.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill and refiners.
stories.eg: Cheaper crude lowers Egypt's import costs.

key.l: EGP per USD, six-bank average sell, midday 23 Nov

stories.h: The pound trades above 54 per dollar; Egypt lands an EV battery plant
stories.what: Six banks quote the dollar at an average of 54.27 buy and 54.37 sell at midday Monday, with ADIB highest at 54.50. Separately, Egypt's first EV battery plant targets production by mid-2027, with a first phase worth more than EGP 2 bn and 1 GWh a year of capacity. Egypt also signs a health compact with the World Bank to extend insurance to about 23.5 mn people by 2030, with about EGP 178 bn of financing.
stories.why: The sources give no reason for the pound's move.
stories.eg: A weaker pound raises import costs; new investment supports industry.
stories.egx: Neutral; mixed for importers and exporters.

key.l: tankers Iran says hit mines near Hormuz

stories.h: Iran says three tankers catch fire after hitting Hormuz mines
stories.what: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers suffered explosions and fires after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's parliament speaker says Tehran will not hold talks until Washington meets seven conditions.
stories.why: The war on Iran continues to target shipping lanes.
stories.aff: Shipping, insurance and Gulf oil flows.
stories.eg: Shipping risk stays high even as oil prices fall.

stories.h: Gold rebounds 2.8% on Monday, then eases; 21K in Egypt slips
stories.what: Spot gold rises 2.8% to settle at $3,635.45 on Monday, then falls 0.3% to $3,625.88 on Tuesday morning. Markets see a December Fed hike as virtually certain. In Egypt, Banky's 21K price falls EGP 40, or 0.70%, to EGP 5,680 a gram on Tuesday.
stories.why: Profit-taking and Fed-hike bets cap gold after Monday's rebound.
stories.eg: Local prices hold near last week's lows.
